name: Bab El Ain & Souks
hero_subtitle: The main entrance to the medina and the doorway to its workshops and markets.

overview.title: Where the Medina Begins
overview.p1: Bab El Ain is one of the main gateways to the old town, and for many visitors the first taste of Chefchaouen. Step through the arch and the noise of the road fades into narrow lanes lined with small shops, workshops and stalls selling local goods.
overview.p2: Look out for hand-woven wool blankets, local goat cheese, olive products, leather goods and simple pottery. Shopkeepers are used to visitors, so browse freely, compare prices and bargain gently. It's a good morning walk that leads naturally uphill towards Place Outa el Hammam.

moods.title: What to Do at Bab El Ain & the Souks
moods.subtitle: A gate, a market and plenty to browse.

1.title: The Gate Itself
1.desc: A photogenic arch that marks the start of the medina. Pause for a few pictures before heading in.

2.title: Blankets, Weaving & Leather
2.desc: Small workshops sell wool, woven goods and leather. Ask about the maker and take your time.

3.title: Cheese, Olives & Honey
3.desc: Try the local goat cheese and stock up on olive products and honey to take home.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Bab El Ain & Souks

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Taxis and buses stop near the gate. Walk in through the arch; the medina itself is car-free.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Mornings are quieter for browsing. Many small shops open later and close for a break in the afternoon.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: Most shops take cash only, and prices are often negotiable. Ask before photographing people or their goods.

q1.question: What is Bab El Ain?
q1.answer: One of the main gates into Chefchaouen's medina, leading into lanes of small shops and workshops.

q2.question: What should I buy in the Chefchaouen souks?
q2.answer: Woven wool blankets, local goat cheese, olive products, honey, leather goods and simple ceramics.

q3.question: Should I haggle?
q3.answer: Gently, yes. Compare a few shops, stay friendly and walk away politely if the price doesn't work.

q4.question: Is Bab El Ain busy?
q4.answer: It gets busy around midday and on weekends. Mornings are calmer.
